title: Wavelets: filter, downsample, and reconstruct selected scales
summary: A discrete wavelet transform separates scales through paired low-pass and high-pass filters. DeTime reconstructs selected coefficient blocks onto the original sample grid.

steps.title: Choose the filter bank
steps.text: The wavelet fixes the analysis and synthesis filters; this trace uses db4.

steps.title: Build the pyramid
steps.text: Low-pass and high-pass filtering are followed by decimation; repeat on the approximation.

steps.title: Select coefficient blocks
steps.text: Retain a block, zero the others, and apply the inverse transform to obtain a sample-aligned contribution.

steps.title: Assign outputs
steps.text: This example assigns A3 to trend and D3+D2 to season; the remainder is input minus those outputs.

parameters.name: wavelet
parameters.effect: Controls filters and their support; db4 has eight analysis taps.

parameters.name: level
parameters.effect: Controls pyramid depth; the example uses three levels.

parameters.name: trend_levels / season_levels
parameters.effect: Indexes the wavedec list [A3,D3,D2,D1] here, not ascending physical scales.

parameters.name: Boundary convention
parameters.effect: The current wrapper uses PyWavelets' default symmetric mode.

cautions: Wavelet detail coefficients are decimated and should not be mistaken for sample-aligned output curves.
Assigning scales to trend or season is an application choice; the transform does not identify physical mechanisms.
The animation uses a safe fixed depth; excessive levels make boundary effects dominate.
trace_note: Computed with PyWavelets 1.10.0; inverse band reconstructions call the current DeTime helper. Moving filter support is a labeled illustration; coefficient values are actual library outputs.
input_note: Deterministic synthetic teaching signal; not a benchmark.
